core_obligations: Fix a fundamental system of open ideals of the ring (proof lines 1346-1347).

Recall that the completion is the limit of the quotients with the limit topology, so that the kernels of the structure maps form a fundamental system of open ideals of the completion (proof lines 1347-1350).
Identify each of those kernels with the closure of the extension of the corresponding ideal, and conclude that the map to the completion is taut (proof lines 1351-1354).
proof_roadmap: The fundamental system of open ideals of the completion (proof lines 1346-1350).
Identification of the kernels with closures (proof lines 1351-1354).
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that for any linearly topologized ring the canonical map to its completion is taut (statement lines 1341-1344). The proof is short and complete: it fixes a fundamental system of open ideals of the ring, recalls that the completion is the limit of the quotients with the limit topology so that the kernels of the structure maps form a fundamental system of open ideals of the completion, and then identifies each of those kernels with the closure of the extension of the corresponding ideal of the ring, which is exactly the condition defining tautness (proof lines 1346-1354). The claim is H2: the argument is brief, but it is a complete derivation in which the relevant system of open ideals of the completion is produced and each member of it is identified with the closure required by the definition, so nothing is left to the reader and no step is a restatement.
